sources.title: Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, 2024-25 BA (Hons) Acting - Audition Process (PDF; the latest BA process document the school's site still serves)
sources.said: Applicants will take part in classes in the following subjects; singing, improvisation, movement, acting and voice and there will also be an interview with the Director of Acting Courses and the Director of Drama. … In this second-round, applicants will be asked to do a third monologue - which has to be a classical piece. … This could be achieved by performing a classical and a contemporary speech, a comedy and a drama piece, or by choosing two different characters. … It will help if you've read the whole play and understand the context of the speech. … Think about who your character is speaking to and where they are. … You will also be asked to do a duologue chosen by the school and sent to the applicant when they are advised that they have passed Stage 1. … Think about what your character is trying to achieve, and see if there is a change of direction in the speech. … Speeches should involve a character close to your own age and at least one speech should be performed in your own accent. … Contrast is important for us to assess your acting potential.

sources.title: Spotlight, 'How Your Specialised Skills Can Make You Stand Out as an Actor', read 2026-10-31
sources.said: Improvisation is a valuable skill that offers many benefits, including enhancing creativity and spontaneity. … Having a range of accents and dialects listed as your special skills will open more doors, especially if you're looking to work in film or do voice work. … Movement strengthens and frees the body, which helps create and bring characters to life. … Period dramas, such as Bridgerton, focus more on acting skills and only require basic dance training, so if you only have a little dance experience, still include it, but be honest about what level you're at. … When selecting special skills for your musical theatre resume, singing is non-negotiable. … Actor-musician roles require actors to sing and play an instrument, and musicals including Hadestown and Once utilise this concept. … Casting directors will often look for comedians when hunting for funny talent. … Other skills to add could include your singing voice type, styles of dance you can perform and if you have a driver's licence. … For many actors, a part in a period drama is the ultimate dream, but knowing how to ride a horse is often required. … Fencing and stage combat are common requirements for stage and screen productions, and many drama schools teach these disciplines. … Stage and screen productions often require actors who speak in a native accent or language to provide authenticity to a role.

sources.title: Guildhall School of Music & Drama, BA Acting Programme and Module Specifications & Assessment Criteria, approved for 2026/27, version published 23/06/2026
sources.said: Part 1: this consists of a group 'warm-up' movement and improvisation session. … experimentation with practical techniques, such as remembering lines or sight- reading … A405 Practice a range of approaches for rehearsal with a director … A401 Practice a range of effective acting techniques … B402 Apply techniques and imagination in response to dramatic situation, demonstrating authenticity and emotional connection in acting … Actors work on their understanding of the character’s need, and explore their imaginative investment in the emotional stakes of a situation. … generation of self-led dramatic work … Different approaches to sight-reading are also explored … Students experiment with how to adopt different behaviors for different dramatic contexts. … B401 Work both collaboratively and autonomously in rehearsal, and respond appropriately to creative approaches … Actors develops specific techniques and practices for embodiment, enabling them to own the words of another as their own, to inhabit the lived experience of another through the imagination … students develop their levels of alertness and responsiveness to dramatic situation, text, space, scene partner and audience. … Students explore punctuation and rhetoric (ethos, logos, pathos, repetition, alliteration, premise, etc.) … Freedom and spontaneity within the actor’s movement potential and the ability to offer and respond to stimuli is specifically addressed. … Students develop the skills required to sustain a variety of roles under professional conditions. … This project explores the demands of working with a play written in verse or poetic form. The work invites students to extend their emotional, vocal and physical energy, range and power. … Phonetics are introduced, with work on identifying and understanding the actor's own accent and individual sound. This lays the foundations to more challenging accent work undertaken in Voice 2. … a freer and more natural use of breath, voice and body; connection with text and dramatic situation; awareness of individual and group space … The work aims to develop students’ ability to embody various rhythms, images and literary devices … A404 Practice a safe and effective range of vocal techniques … Audio: this component explores a variety of vocal recorded media such as radio drama, commercials, audiobooks, animation and voice acting for gaming. … working in a recording studio including: microphone technique and technical vocal issues (the adapted control of breath, volume, inflection) … This leads on to more intensive work on range, resonance, support and articulation. … Speech Systems: this component develops methods of analysing various Speech Systems. … this component develops students to become self-sufficient in warming up their voices safely and effectively … A voice reel which will consist of a piece of dramatic text or prose and a commercial lasting between 3-4 minutes … A403 Practice a safe and effective range of movement techniques … Skills are explored to develop the expressivity required for physical transformation and characterisation. … The student is asked to take the space as a soloist, as well as working with an accompanist. … This component develops students’ sense of rhythm and musicality as well as strengthening their vocal instrument. … This is to assess the applicant’s ability to perform and interpret a song, rather than their singing ability. The panel will specifically be looking for the applicant’s ability to connect to the language and realise dramatic situation within the song. … Safe practices are explored in the creation of cross-cultural dance and dramatic violence … A402 Understand the fundamentals of acting on screen … Students are required to produce a self-tape in response to a brief set by the Screen Acting tutor. … become familiar with the terminology of screen work and the various roles of key members of a film crew. … explores the specific technical demands of working on set including maintaining continuity, working with marks, eye lines, understanding different lens sizes, and managing energy and concentration. … meeting some of the professional challenges related to intensive filming schedules, time-pressures and extensive independent preparation. … The criteria on which the panels makes their decision are: believability, connection and commitment, demonstrated in the audition and interview, and focus, enthusiasm and potential to benefit from the programme. … The project invites students to integrate believability with stagecraft. … The criteria on which the panels makes their decision are: believability, connection and commitment, demonstrated in the audition and interview … B502 Integrate techniques and imagination in response to an advanced range of dramatic situations and repertoire, demonstrating expressiveness in acting … A407 Understand critical perspectives on relevant debates in relation to performance … and focus, enthusiasm and potential to benefit from the programme … C402* Identify a range of research and composition skills for structuring and communicating ideas … Practices from across continents enhance and increase strength, stamina, agility and movement potential. … The exploration of the actor’s body promotes wellbeing, self-care and supports the development of strength, co-ordination and flexibility. … D501* Utilise efficient personal organisation skills for a demanding work schedule … C401* Practice an appropriate range of methodologies for self- reflection … C603 Evidence a range of skills in order to be an effective practitioner, with capacity to lead and yield … C403* Practice the skills required to work safely and effectively as part of a group … D502 Prepare effectively for professional opportunities … D602 Evidence a strategic approach to career development, assimilating an effective range of skills with knowledge of the industry … A603 Evidence creative and industry knowledge and apply this to opportunities that replicate industry practice
